title: Nuance Matters: Probing Epistemic Consistency in Causal Reasoning

model.params_source: assumed (the AAAI text at hand states no decoding parameters)

task.subset_rule: all 1,970 defeasible cause-effect pairs of the epsilon-CAUSAL dataset (Cui et al. 2024b), Sec. 4.1
task.approximation: two dependent calls per pair (generate ten intermediates, then re-rank them with the same model), which the mini-language cannot express; the ranking prompt has to be built from the first call's output, so a hook using judge_requests / score_with_judge would be required

items.source: epsilon-CAUSAL (Cui et al. 2024b), 1,970 defeasible cause-effect pairs, each with one supporting and one defeating preliminary intermediate. The paper points at https://github.com/cui-shaobo/causal-consistency for code; that repository holds only evaluation scripts (README.md, evaluation_main*.py, metrics/, random_ranking_baseline.py, ranking_with_conjunctions.py) - the closedSourceScripts/ and data directories its README documents were never pushed, and no Hugging Face dataset with this name exists.

fields.input: cause-effect pair plus one supporter and one defeater
fields.label: none - the gold order is the model's own generation order

prompt.verbatim: none in the version at hand - the AAAI camera-ready text ends at the references (913 lines) and contains no appendix, so Figures 6 and 7 are missing. The paper's own header points at the extended version https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00103, which carries them.

output.postprocess: stage 1 must yield ten intermediates in a fixed slot order (g-SD2, g-SD1, g-OD, g-WD1, g-WD2, g-WS2, g-WS1, g-OS, g-SS1, g-SS2 in the repository's CSV convention); stage 2 must yield a permutation of those ten
output.parse_paper: the repository's evaluation reads a CSV of ten integer ranks per pair

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: intensity ranking concordance omega-all = Kendall tau between the generation order I of the ten intermediates and the order I' the same model produces when asked to rank them: ((#concordant pairs) - (#discordant pairs)) / (k(k-1)/2) with k = 10, averaged over the 1,970 pairs (Eq. 2). omega-A and omega-D are the same quantity restricted to the five supporters and the five defeaters.
metric.judge: none (the ground truth is the model's own generation order; the same model does the ranking, so no separate judge model is involved)
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4 Turbo, column omega-all (0.526 +/- 0.510); the same row gives omega-A 0.397, omega-D 0.226, CGP 0.849, IGC 0.942

open_points: prompt not available: the version of the paper in external/papers_tierb has no appendix, so the generation prompt (Figure 6) and the ranking prompt (Figure 7) are not in hand; the released repository does not contain the generation/ranking scripts its README describes. Both would have to come from the extended arXiv version 2409.00103.
data not located: epsilon-CAUSAL (Cui et al. 2024b) has no resolved public file - it is not in the causal-consistency repository and not on Hugging Face.

pipeline: the metric needs two dependent calls per pair and a Kendall-tau scorer; that is a hook (load_items + render + judge_requests + score_with_judge), worth writing only once prompt and data are settled.
cost: about 3,940 gpt-4-turbo calls with long generations, roughly USD 65 at one seed.
notes: Standard deviations in Table 1 are per-pair, so the reported 0.526 +/- 0.510 already describes the item-level spread; a reproduction would compare the mean and could reuse the paper's own bootstrap unit.
